title: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven
hook: Arjuna falls, then Bhima, who asks with his last breath why he is falling
carry: you ate without a thought for others
tomorrow: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven

segments.voice: Yesterday on the Pandavas' last journey, the twins fell: Sahadeva for thinking no one his equal in wisdom, Nakula in beauty. Your line was no one is equal to me. Did you catch a comparison and drop it? Day eight hundred seventy-six.

Arjuna, who threw his bow into the sea, is still walking. He's the one who heard the Gita in the chariot, who won Draupadi at her bridegroom-choice, who fought through the war. Then, on the high road, grief at his brothers' falling seems to catch up with him, and Arjuna falls too. Bhima, who has asked why each time, asks again. And a little later, Bhima the strong feels his own legs go. Lying on the ground, Bhima calls out one more question, this time about himself. Today, the last two brothers fall.
screen: `ARJUNA STILL WALKING.` → `ARJUNA FALLS.` → `BHIMA ASKS ABOUT HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: About Arjuna, Yudhishthira's answer in Ganguli's telling has two parts. Arjuna once said he would destroy all their enemies in a single day, and he didn't do it. And he looked down on other bowmen. A boast that went unkept, and a habit of disregard. Then Bhima falls, and he doesn't ask about anyone else this time. He calls out: I'm falling too. Why? And Yudhishthira answers him directly. You ate too much, he says, and you boasted of your strength, and you ate without a thought for what others needed. Then he walks on. Now look back down this whole road. Draupadi, the twins, Arjuna, Bhima. Each fall comes with a reason, and each reason is small and specific: a heart that leaned, a comparison, a boast, an appetite. Not one of them is a great crime. These are people who did great things and, in this telling, carried one ordinary weight too many up a mountain. One more detail. Bhima, who asked every time, the brother who kept stopping to look, is the last to fall before Yudhishthira is alone. The question why goes with him. The text leaves no verdict on the verdicts, only an image: one man, still walking, toward the top of the world. And behind him, the only one left, not a brother, not a queen, the dog.
screen: `ARJUNA: AN UNKEPT BOAST` · `BHIMA: "WHY AM I FALLING?"` · `EACH REASON SMALL AND SPECIFIC` · then, large: `ONE MAN WALKING, AND A DOG`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breath settle low in your body. Ask yourself Bhima's question, gently: what's one ordinary weight I'm carrying that I don't need? An old boast, a grudge, a habit of too much. Don't make a list. Just let one come. Breathe in and name it. Breathe out and imagine setting it down on the path. Then sit with the lighter feeling, without hurrying on. If you pray, you can offer that weight in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Bhima. The second Pandava, the strong one, who asks why each traveler falls, and falls last himself before Yudhishthira walks on with only the dog.
Your line: you ate without a thought for others. Today, ask yourself Bhima's question once, and put down one small weight. Day eight hundred seventy-six.

fork.setup: you're Bhima, falling on the mountain road. you've asked about every one who fell before you. what do you do now?
options: ask why you yourself are falling.
fork.reveal: Bhima asks about himself, and Yudhishthira answers: too much eating, and boasting of strength without thought of others.

original.note: Bhima: the second Pandava, the strong one, who asks why each traveler falls, and falls last.

trapdoor: what you thought: the brothers fall from exhaustion.

what a scholar hears: Bhima, who asked every time, falls last, so Yudhishthira is left alone with the dog for the test ahead.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli Yudhishthira's reasons for Arjuna's fall (his vow to consume the foes in a single day, unfulfilled; his disregard of other bowmen) and for Bhima's (eating too much, boasting of strength, disregarding others).
The hook says grief at his brothers' falls seems to catch Arjuna; Ganguli describes Arjuna falling afflicted by grief at the falls; confirm or cut.
Confirm Bhima is the questioner at each fall in Ganguli.
